newsitem.title: CHINA: China defence industry shows higher profits in '96.
newsitem.headline: China defence industry shows higher profits in '96.

text.p: China's top 100 military enterprises reported profit growth last year of 9.2 percent but must adapt to the marketplace to ensure they remain in the black, Vice Premier Wu Bangguo has said.
Last year, the output value of China's key 100 military enterprises grew by 8.2 percent while turnover rose by 10.9 percent, the Economic Daily said on Wednesday.
However, Wu told a meeting on military industries in Beijing that much more needed to be done if the sprawling business sector of China's People's Liberation Army was to make money.
"Military enterprises should improve management and efficiency," he was quoted as saying.
Because the market environment had seen huge changes, enterprises must change their management methods and operations to keep pace, Wu said.

"The central government and local governments at different levels will support the reforms and development of military enterprises in the same the way they treat civilian enterprises," the newspaper quoted Wu as saying.
China's military has hundreds of enterprises with civilian products accounting for about 80 percent of the total industrial output of China's military companies in 1995.

Chinese figures show the declared profit of the People's Liberation Army in 1993 was $1.0 billion on turnover of $6-9 billion, but military analysts believe its real profits were at least double that from an industry that has been transformed into an economic powerhouse in the last decade.

Beijing announced on Sunday it was throwing open the doors to its defence industry to foreign investors in an about-face aimed at ensuring it has the high-tech weaponry needed to fight battles of the future.

Commanders of its backward but secretive defence sector, drawing lessons from the Gulf War, have endorsed a plan to let foreign companies join in defence electronics next year -- rather than fall even further behind.
